chapter: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
title: Erroll Garner at Tondelayo's and joining Local 802
summary: Ramirez admired Erroll Garner's chords, introduced him in Willie Bryant days, and helped him join the union after Bill Bailey objected.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: As I said before, we were working that night at Tondelayo's(?), and Erroll... Erroll was so magnificent a player. I mean, I never saw anybody handle chords on the keyboard like him at that time. The more he played, the more he liked to play, and the fact that I was listening to him made him go on more and more and more.

Anyhow, as I said before, I got very interested in the axe/acts(?) after... I would start playing... To play a dance (?) and try to do anything, you'd have to be there all night and sweat about a lot...you know, sweat plenty anyhow. Anyway, we became very good friends. And of course, Linton throughout the years... When I was with Hot Lips Page, we used to be on the road together. His brother, Linton, by the way, is no slouch on piano, you know.

Anyhow, it seems to me I... At the time I played the Apollo again, and I think...I don't know, I remember... Now, this is before...back in the Willie Bryant days. It was the first time I met Erroll. And during the time, during the acts, I used to play for Bill Bailey, who was Pearl Bailey's brother. Of course, we struck a nice relationship, more or
less. You know, the band would stop and I would play for Bill. He had this beautiful routine; he was quite a dancer.

There came a time, though, I told him... I said there's a piano player outside there; he wanted to get in the union. That was Erroll. I said, "Have him play for you, let him play for you and I'll take a rest with the band." He says, "Okay." So I got Erroll to play for Bill. When Bill came back, he says, "Oh no, man, I don't want him to play for me." "Why not?" Well, the fact remains that Erroll was just so superb that he was taking the spot away from Bill! If Bill does a routine, Erroll would do it on the piano, you know, and everything like that. It was just much too competitive. Of course, at the time there was a union delegate named Redman, and Erroll had to have a voucher to get into the union, and I helped him to get into the Local 802. He didn't forget that.
So getting back to Tondelayo's(?), we used to talk about that. We had a pretty nice thing going there at Tondelayo's(?). After that I just...
